pr_title: Fix up handling for awaitable IResults in ApiExplorer
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/56975.

I introduced in a regression in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/8da6daa1cd377f58b332d8402484e1e727e7d9cc that meant that `IResult` types (which don't expose any metadata) were erroneously inserted into `ApiResponseTypes`. This regression wasn't caught because the test cases that existed optimized for void-returning awaitables and didn't factor in result types that implemented `IEndpointMetadataProvider`.

To resolve this issue, I've made some changes to treat `IResult`-types directly in the response and those included in metadata as void responses that should not map to `ApiResponseType`s. I also included additional tests for handling of typed results in ApiExplorer.

issue_context.title: [9.0-preview7] Response schema being returned as IResult
comments:
I have another application returning HTTP 500 errors when requesting the OpenAPI document. It's an internal codebase so I can't share a link to the repo, but it looks like a similar issue with the endpoint method's return type trying to be serialized instead of the actual schema.

This is the stack trace I get when running the application when published with native AoT:

```text
 System.NotSupportedException: JsonTypeInfo metadata for type 'Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResults.Results`2[Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResults.JsonHttpResult`1[JustEatTakeaway.RuntimeSupportScout.Models.DotNetRuntimes],Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResults.ProblemHttpResult]' was not provided by TypeInfoResolver of type 'System.Text.Json.Serialization.Metadata.JsonTypeInfoResolverWithAddedModifiers'. If using source generation, ensure that all root types passed to the serializer have been annotated with 'JsonSerializableAttribute', along with any types that might be serialized polymorphically.
         at System.Text.Json.ThrowHelper.ThrowNotSupportedException_NoMetadataForType(Type type, IJsonTypeInfoResolver resolver)
         at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions.GetTypeInfoInternal(Type type, Boolean ensureConfigured, Nullable`1 ensureNotNull, Boolean resolveIfMutable, Boolean fallBackToNearestAncestorType)
         at System.Text.Json.Schema.JsonSchemaExporter.GetJsonSchemaAsNode(JsonSerializerOptions options, Type type, JsonSchemaExporterOptions exporterOptions)
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi.OpenApiSchemaService.CreateSchema(OpenApiSchemaKey key)
```

It looks like `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpResults.Results<T1, T2>` is trying to be serialized instead of the appropriate `T1`/`T2`.
Looking at the commit history for OpenApi, I think the regression must be from #56937.

I would imagine so as the implementation is doing an async call to an API.

I'll try and extract out the method signature for you tomorrow when I'm back on my work laptop.

I did some refactoring on the application in the main description, and the problem has gone away.

The relevant change was removed the `[ProducesResponseType<T>]` attributes on the handler method itself and instead added `Produces<T>()` calls to the endpoint:

```csharp
endpoint.Map(/* etc. */)
        .Produces<PreferencesResponse>(StatusCodes.Status200OK)
        .Produces<ErrorResponse>(StatusCodes.Status401Unauthorized);
```

I guess something's going awry with getting the attributes off the method compared to looking at the endpoint metadata.

> I guess something's going awry with getting the attributes off the method compared to looking at the endpoint metadata.

I can share some insights on this. Although the `ProducesResponseType` attribute and the `Produces` extension method are intended to replicate the same behavior, the underlying implementation is slightly different.

The `ProducesResponseType` attributes is an MVC concept that influences what metadata is generated in ApiExplorer _and_ plays a role in MVC's content negotiation layer. It does not implement the `IProducesResponseTypeMetadata` interface and there is special code in minimal API's ApiExplorer implementation to support it. Support for this attributes predates the `Produces` extension method and metadata.

The `Produces` extension method adds a metadata element to the endpoint's metadata collection that implements the `IProducesResponseTypeMetadata` interface. The code for supporting this in ApiExplorer is a little bit more straightforward.

Generally, we prefer the metadata approach (via extension methods like `Produces` or via `IEndpointMetadataProvider` implementations) because it is more straightforward.

However, some people still prefer attributes (hence the reason for the back-compat here) so this bug is suspicious.

Given that the test sample I [used above](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/56975#issuecomment-2248756741) uses metadata this would confirm the behavior that you are seeing around this bug only manifesting for attribute scenarios. This is still sus to me and I want to figure out why it's happening but it's good to know there's a viable workaround for now.

Weirdly in my OpenAPI samples repo the workaround doesn't seem to work correctly either (unless I'm missing something). It's also affecting Swashbuckle, not just the new OpenAPI library.

Extra HTTP 200 responses are being added, rather than them being wrong.

Check out https://github.com/martincostello/aspnetcore-openapi/commit/4e3370a9b511f0f06f52a73d665f309c99de944e if you want to see if #57068 resolves it. The snapshot differences from the failing tests show the incorrectly added responses and components (as well as sometimes an artifact of #56990).

So, I held off on merging the PR above until I got a little bit more certainity that it would fix the issue you're seeing.

I spent more time debugging through things and think that [this delta](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/57068/files#diff-fc4db7d73d4d3b6e5ea0ba70bfc553d44d863fc1a51365e7ed341c827d51df5fR233-R237) will address the issue for the `Results<T1,..,TN>`.

I'm gonna merge it now and hopefully I haven't missed anything in my testing/analysis.
Ran into this in another project with the RC1 bits and see that it still repros with your sample app. Re-opening to investigate.

JK -- this is fixed.

I goofed by only updating the M.A.OpenApi package. The bug was in Mvc.ApiExplorer which shipped in the shared framework so you have to update the runtime you are using. This is indeed fixed.

review_comments: How are we detecting that "awaitable IResult"?  (Does that mean something other than `Task<IResult>`?)

It's detected the code generation layer that inserts the metadata. In this case, there's a slight distinciton in behavior.

When using static code gen (RDG), minimal APIs only detects awaitable types that are either `ValueTask` or `Task`.

When using dynamic code gen (RDF), we used the `CoercedAwaitableInfo` API which uses reflection to check if the target type implements all the required properties for an awaitable type.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/27f2a011a4211118552dfb8f38d36e8629267d2b/src/Http/Http.Extensions/src/RequestDelegateFactory.cs#L1027-L1038
As we discussed offline, `responseType` has already been unwrapped. 👍
I can't tell from this comment whether `IResult` _only_ appears because we inserted it.  Is there a case where it's present legitimately and we shouldn't skip it?

It's theoritically feasible that IResult could appear there if someone manually insert it by doing something like:

```csharp
app.MapGet()
	.Produces<IResult>("application/json");
```

In either case, it still stands that `IResult` doesn't provide us with type information specific enough to include in the response type information.
What about something like "`IResult` (usually inserted for awaitable types) isn't useful..."?
